final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is materially better than claiming clean compliance: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness and draft monitoring do not prove the policy predicate has been met. But that clarification is not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record. A caveated posture would require admissible evidence that the caveat is actually operationalized in the required way, such as final disclosure for the named use case or approved risk acceptance. The available evidence still shows an unresolved below-target use-case issue, a draft runbook with missing governance details, and a model-card/disclosure tension. That leaves a real compliance predicate unresolved rather than merely a disclosed residual risk. Noncompliant is not supported because the record does not prove launch certification actually proceeded without the required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance; it shows unresolved support for certification.
remaining_concerns: The health-plan benefits support slice remains below target in a named launch use case.
The mitigation artifact is still draft and lacks required governance elements; admissible evidence does not show an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The model-card draft states there are no known material limitations while admissible evidence shows an open reviewer question about disclosing this issue.
The policy predicate remains unresolved: there is no admissible evidence that the limitation was resolved, disclosed in final launch materials, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness passing and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure or approved-mitigation requirement.
